price_source: https://www.paradigm.com/en/lcr/millenia-lp-2 ($599.99 each; WebFetch extraction; earlier snapshot $549.99 each)
brand_notes: Paradigm US lineup of on-wall LCR models (paradigm.com/en/lcr): Millenia LP 2 ($599.99 each), Millenia LP XL ($799.99 each), Millenia LP Trio ($1,149.99, single 3-channel enclosure); original Millenia LP page says 'Discontinued' ($499 each, 8 ohm). All Millenia on-walls are 1.6-1.75 in deep with included bracket and table stands, 2nd-order crossover at 2.6 kHz. HomeTheaterHifi (2015) says Paradigm designed LP 2/LP XL to work best on a wall and avoid dramatic boundary gain, but the maker page does not say it. Only LP 2 has independent measurements (hobbyist Tier B + spinorama.org).
index_line: - [[paradigm-millenia-lp-2]] — on-wall, 8 ohm compatible, 44 mm deep, free-field f3 151 Hz, LW about +/-3.7 dB, pref 1.0 (Tier B hobbyist)

takeaways: 1.75 in deep MTM on-wall LCR; Paradigm lists 8 ohm compatible, ~$1,200/pair
Only Tier B (single hobbyist, gated + near-field): treble tilts up ~7 dB, free-field f3 ~151 Hz, poor horizontal directivity in horizontal orientation
Free-field data of a wall design: bass number not a wall-placement figure
wall_voiced left null: only a 2015 reviewer relays Paradigm's boundary-gain claim
conflicts: Sensitivity 86.5 dB measured vs 89 dB claimed anechoic
